done_when: A follow-up that names a period answers for that period whatever window the model emits; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: The fallback still does not deterministically resolve every explicitly named period. For example, after a July 2026 answer, “What about 2025?” names an unambiguous year, but neither parser recognizes a year alone and `hasTimePeriodWords` returns false, so line 391 removes even a correct model window and the later inheritance restores July 2026. Conversely, “Show Q3” is classified as period language but cannot be parsed without an explicit year, so a wrong model-emitted window survives unchanged. Thus explicit periods do not win whatever window the model emits, as required.
findings.title: Not done: Named periods must override the model; no-period turns must inherit/aggregate; edited periods must rerun as chosen

findings.body: The added regression scenarios call `ChatService.ask` directly with fake model, executor, warehouse, and audit boundaries. Repository inspection found no Playwright test/configuration or browser test command covering a named-period follow-up, no-period inheritance/aggregation, and changing an answer’s period. The existing frontend tests also mock the Ask API. Consequently, this user-facing behavior remains proven only by unit/component tests rather than through a browser, running API, real database, prior-turn transport, and period control as required.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
